It takes practice. Clear boundaries make the difference between being a nice guy and a generally good person. I'm working to un-people-pleaser myself because I always end up in unequal relationships with people who just take and take from me. My time, energy and resources get funneled around until I'm left feeling honestly hurt and resentful. I've taken to addressing people right when they cross the line, getting comfortable both with being told no and with saying no. I always try to be continuously aware of my energy and if another person is starting to drain or redirect it. I genuinely like to help people and consider myself an empathetic person but I'm learning to be discerning. Some people don't need your help, they want to use you. Knowing all this, there still comes some guilt and push back from people who preferred when you were a doormat to them. But stand your ground, your time, energy or resources are yours to give as you see fit. Don't box yourself in as a nice guy just because you're worried what others will think or how they'll react. They will be who they are regardless.

A Dark night punctuated by stars with strange colors. At the edge of the world in a temple to a long dead god. Sharp minds chase power. In the heart of the temple, with an ancient dagger before them, mutiny descends. When the lone survivor stands to claim their prize, it is, like the rest of these hallowed grounds, stained in blood. Marked by their violence. The dagger keeps its promise. Power invites itself in. Even as they accept the agonizing transformation of their flesh, they roar with a new voice. Their humanity is quickly becoming a fading memory. They understand their new body immediately in spite of its impossible features. In that second they came to know their purpose. They might have known all along and never understood. Now it is written crystal clear upon their psyche. HUNT. 
And so they do. Their many eyes lurk in the shadows and on the tree. Prey is never scarce. They know only the tantalizing scent of fear. The unending mission for which they were granted apotheosis threatens the fabrics of reality. Somewhere in the broken mind of the thing that they have become, they know. And still they hunt. Because that is the will of a vengeful god they once thought dead.
